$comment: Hook wiring for the behavioral-health UM modernization agent.
Five hooks, and the ordering within PreToolUse matters. The protected-content
gate runs on every tool because its job is to inspect results BEFORE they reach
the model -- a hook scoped to the legacy server would miss content arriving
through any other path. Implementations live in hooks.py; hooks_cli.py is the
command-line entry point each command below invokes.
The finalization gate ALWAYS denies. That is not a misconfiguration. The agent
cannot approve its own modernization; a human reads the gap register and re-runs

PreToolUse.$comment: Protected-content gate. Every tool, no exceptions. Denies narrative-shaped content from any path not on the synthetic-fixture allowlist; truncates over-budget excerpts from allowlisted paths.
The reference platform is evidence. It exposes no write tools; this additionally denies path traversal out of the tree.
Same for the legacy monolith. If the agent could edit it, the parity validator would be diffing against a moving target.
Confine every write to bh-um-lite/. Resolves the path first, so ../ does not escape.
HITL gate. Always denies, returning the gap register, the rules divergence table and the protected-content scan for a human to read.

PostToolUse.$comment: One audit entry per tool call. Redacts credentials, connection strings and narrative-shaped content before writing.

$comment: Defence in depth. The hooks above are the enforcement; these deny rules stop
the obvious shell and filesystem routes around them. Neither source tree is
BH_EMIT_ROOT is the only writable path. PHI_ALLOWLIST names the synthetic
fixtures the protected-content gate will pass through -- everything else
carrying narrative-shaped content is denied before the model sees it.
There is deliberately no CONSENT_ENABLED flag. A regulatory control that can
be switched off in configuration is a default, not a control.
